Plot community types

Source: R/community_types.r
plot.ecodive_types.Rd

Draws a result of enterotype() or valencia() with base graphics.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'ecodive_types'
plot(x, type = c("profiles", "selection", "scores"), n_features = 10, ...)

Arguments

x

A result of enterotype() or valencia().

type

"profiles", "selection" or "scores".

n_features

The number of features to show in "profiles". Default 10.

...

Passed on to graphics::barplot(), graphics::plot.default() or graphics::boxplot(), such as main, ylab or col.

Value

x, invisibly.

Details

  • "profiles" (the default): stacked bars of each type's composition (for enterotype(), its samples' mean proportions; for valencia(), the centroids), with the n_features features that reach the largest proportion in any type, and the rest pooled as "Other". The bars are labelled with the type and its number of samples.

  • "selection": the criterion that chose the number of types (for enterotype(), the Calinski-Harabasz index) against the number of types, with the one chosen circled. Not for valencia(), whose centroids fix the types.

  • "scores" (valencia() only): boxplots of the samples' scores (their similarity to their sub-CST's centroid), one per sub-CST with samples, in VALENCIA's colours, each beside a diamond and bar for the mean \(\pm\) standard deviation of VALENCIA's reference samples, as VALENCIA's own plot shows them.

The types keep the order of levels(x$type) in every plot.

Examples

    et <- enterotype(iris[, 1:4], n_types = 2:5)
    plot(et)

    plot(et, 'selection')


    # VALENCIA on thirteen samples made from its centroids.
    counts <- round(valencia_centroids * 10000)
    rownames(counts) <- paste0('S', 1:13)
    vl <- valencia(counts)
    plot(vl)

    plot(vl, 'scores')
